prompt:
A small metal ring of negligible mass is held in equilibrium at the origin by three coplanar tension forces:
- Tension P = 60.0 N acting horizontally to the right along the positive x-axis
- Tension S = 80.0 N acting vertically downwards along the negative y-axis
- Tension Q acting at an angle theta above the negative x-axis (into the second quadrant)
[FIGURE PLACEHOLDER: Free-body force diagram at origin O. Horizontal vector P = 60.0 N to the right (+x). Downward vertical vector S = 80.0 N (-y). Diagonal vector Q directed up and to the left, making angle theta above the negative x-axis.]

(a) State the condition for the forces acting on the ring to be in equilibrium. [1]
(b) By resolving forces horizontally, write an equation relating P and the horizontal component of Q, and deduce the horizontal component of Q. [1]
(c) By resolving forces vertically, write an equation relating S and the vertical component of Q, and deduce the vertical component of Q. [1]
(d) Calculate the magnitude of force Q. [1]
(e) Calculate the angle theta that force Q makes with the horizontal. [1]
(f) State the magnitude and direction of the resultant of forces P and S alone. [1]

answer.text:
(a) The resultant force on the ring must be zero (or the vector sum of all forces is zero, Sigma F = 0).
(b) Q * cos(theta) = P = 60.0 N (horizontal component of Q is 60.0 N to the left).
(c) Q * sin(theta) = S = 80.0 N (vertical component of Q is 80.0 N upwards).
(d) Q = sqrt(60.0^2 + 80.0^2) = sqrt(3600 + 6400) = sqrt(10000) = 100 N.
(e) tan(theta) = 80.0 / 60.0 = 1.333, so theta = 53.1 degrees above the negative x-axis.
(f) Magnitude = 100 N; direction is at 53.1 degrees below the positive x-axis (directly opposite to Q).

hints: Equilibrium means there is no acceleration, so the net force must be zero.
mark_scheme: 1 mark: Resultant force is zero / sum of coplanar forces equals zero.
9702_t01_cm05_l11_theory09_a.solution: The resultant force acting on the ring must be zero.

hints: Rightward forces must balance leftward forces: P = Q * cos(theta).
mark_scheme: 1 mark: Q * cos(theta) = 60.0 N (or horizontal component = 60.0 N to the left).
9702_t01_cm05_l11_theory09_b.solution: Horizontal equilibrium: Q * cos(theta) = P = 60.0 N.

hints: Upward forces must balance downward forces: Q * sin(theta) = S.
mark_scheme: 1 mark: Q * sin(theta) = 80.0 N (or vertical component = 80.0 N upwards).
9702_t01_cm05_l11_theory09_c.solution: Vertical equilibrium: Q * sin(theta) = S = 80.0 N.

hints: Combine the horizontal and vertical components of Q using Pythagoras.

mark_scheme: 1 mark: theta = arctan(80.0 / 60.0) = 53.1 degrees (above negative x-axis).

hints: For equilibrium, P + S + Q = 0, which means (P + S) = -Q.
mark_scheme: 1 mark: Magnitude = 100 N, direction directly opposite to Q (53.1 degrees below positive x-axis).
9702_t01_cm05_l11_theory09_f.solution: Resultant of P and S has magnitude 100 N and points in the exact opposite direction to Q (53.1 degrees below the positive x-axis).

hints: In equilibrium, components along each axis sum to zero.
Use Pythagoras on the perpendicular components to find the magnitude of Q.
The resultant of any two forces in a three-force equilibrium must equal and oppose the third force.
solution:
(a) Resultant force is zero.
(b) Q * cos(theta) = 60.0 N.
(c) Q * sin(theta) = 80.0 N.
(d) Q = sqrt(60.0^2 + 80.0^2) = 100 N.
(e) theta = arctan(80.0 / 60.0) = 53.1 degrees.
(f) Magnitude = 100 N, direction directly opposite to Q.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: Part (a): state condition: resultant force is zero (1 mark).
Step 2: Part (b): resolve horizontally: Q_x = P = 60.0 N (1 mark).
Step 3: Part (c): resolve vertically: Q_y = S = 80.0 N (1 mark).
Step 4: Part (d): recombine Q = sqrt(60^2 + 80^2) = 100 N (1 mark).
Step 5: Part (e): angle theta = arctan(80 / 60) = 53.1 degrees (1 mark).
Step 6: Part (f): recognize that P + S = -Q, so resultant has magnitude 100 N opposite to Q (1 mark).
